body.heading: An open sign on the reef
paragraphs: Cleaner shrimp set up at regular spots on the reef, sometimes called cleaning stations, and advertise with slow, waving movements of their white antennae. Fish that would normally eat a shrimp instead hover quietly and wait their turn.

The shrimp climb over their clients, picking off dead skin, mucus and tiny parasites. They will even venture inside an open mouth or under the gill covers of large fish, places where a small creature would expect to become lunch.

body.heading: A deal both sides keep
paragraphs: This partnership is a form of symbiosis: a close, lasting relationship between two different species. The shrimp get a reliable food supply delivered to their door. The fish get grooming that removes parasites and damaged tissue, which helps keep them healthy.

Trust is the whole system. A predator that ate its cleaner would lose the service forever, and fish that cheat are rare. The arrangement works because, over many visits, honesty pays better than a single meal.

takeaway: Cleaner shrimp and reef fish trade food for grooming in a partnership built on repeated trust.
